text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 — auth-service: token verification error rate spike (>= 70% 401s) · page fired to oncall

pagerduty: Incident: auth-service JWT validation failures — high error rate. Trigger rule: auth.jwt.validation.errors > 50/min.

Alex Chen: acked. I'm on it. Jumping into logs and metrics now.

Darren O'Neal: seeing the same from synthetic checks — login flows failing, /v1/token verify returning 401 with 'invalid_kid' and 'no matching key' in logs.

Alex Chen: grabbing recent deploys — any cert/key rotation in last 30m? @infra-bot any automation?

infra-bot: No infra deploys in last 2h. Key-rotation job ran 04:12 UTC yesterday only.

Julie Park: customer reports coming in — OAuth logins and API auth for some customers failing. Flags in support queue with several customers impacted.

Sam Patel: I'm available for escalation if you want to hand off. Could be JWKS propagation issue or signer switched keys.

Alex Chen: logs from auth-signer: 
```
[2026-03-14T03:01:02Z] JWT_VERIFY ERROR kid abc123 not found in JWKS
[2026-03:01:35Z] upstream jwks fetch status=200, keys=1
[2026-03:01:35Z] loaded_key_kid=def456
```
This suggests signer or token issuer used kid=abc123 but JWKS only has def456.

Darren O'Neal: I can query the JWKS endpoint from prod control plane: `curl -s https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'` returns ["def456"].

Alex Chen: timeline hypothesis: signer rotated (or a canary) produced tokens with new kid (abc123) but JWKS endpoint not updated / not propagated to edge caches. Or tokens were issued by a staged signer.

Sam Patel: Check the signing service instances: `kubectl get pods -n auth -l app=signer -o wide` and check env var SIGNING_KEY_KID on each pod. Also certs in KMS?

Alex Chen: running checks. One signer pod shows SIGNING_KEY_KID=abc123 but uploader job failed with 500 when calling JWKS publish. Recent logs from jwks-uploader show 500 from storage backend: `POST /jwks publish -> 500: Key upload failed`

Julie Park: support: impact summary so far — about 11% of active tokens failing (region eu-west-1 mostly), about 800 401s/min across customer-facing APIs, some SSO flows timing out. Potential active customer sessions impacted.

Darren O'Neal: Could we temporarily point backend verification to accept both def456 and abc123 from a fallback key store? Is there a cached JWKS we can use?

Alex Chen: Two immediate mitigations: 1) re-publish the missing JWKS key (if we have the public key archived) 2) roll signer pods back to previous key (def456) by changing SIGNING_KEY_KID -> def456 and restart pods. Which is faster?

Sam Patel: If jwks-uploader is failing due to storage 500, re-publishing might still fail. Rolling signer config to old key is quick if key material present locally or in KMS. We need to confirm KMS has def456 private key access.

Alex Chen: I can do a quick rollback to def456 on one pod to validate. Will patch deployment with `kubectl set env deploy/auth-signer SIGNING_KEY_KID=def456 --namespace=auth` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-signer`. Testing on canary instance first.

infra-bot: Note: rolling restart will create new pod; watch for increased auth CPU due to cache warmup.

(5min later)

Alex Chen: Can confirm canary restarted with def456 and issuing tokens now show kid=def456. Verified login succeeds for that canary. Rolling the rest now.

Julie Park: Support: seeing drop in open tickets for region eu-west-1, customers reporting auth is returning to normal intermittently. Marking impacted customers as 'monitoring'.

security: quick question — do we have evidence tokens with abc123 were issued maliciously? Or a bad rollout? We need to rotate if private key leaked.

Alex Chen: No evidence of leak. Likely misconfiguration in deployment pipeline triggered alternate key. We'll treat as potential operational error until proven otherwise.

Darren O'Neal: After rolling restarts, error rate from 401s dropped from 800/min to ~20/min over 12 minutes. JWKS uploader still returning 500.

Sam Patel: For safety, I'm going to escalate to platform infra to fix jwks-uploader backend (storage 500). Assigning to infra oncall.

infra-bot: infra-oncall notified: pagerduty ticket PD-98765.

Alex Chen: Moving incident to mitigated state for token verification — majority of traffic back to normal. We'll keep pager open until jwks-uploader fixed and we confirm no further drift.

Julie Park: Customer impact summary (to include in incident page): Partial outage for auth token verification, intermittent for ~40 minutes, primarily EU region, impacted SSO and API token flows, estimated 25% of requests were returning 401 at peak, resolved by rolling signer back to previous key. Next steps: postmortem, fix deployment logic to prevent inadvertent key switch, add healthcheck for JWKS publish, add alert for jwks-uploader failures.

Sam Patel: I'll take first oncall handoff and monitor for 2h, then hand to Darren for long-term follow-up and postmortem writeup.

Alex Chen: Thanks all. I'll capture the runbook steps used and paste into incident timeline. Key actions: `kubectl set env`, `kubectl rollout restart`, verify `curl /.well-known/jwks.json`, monitor 401 rate.

Alex Chen: Runbook snippet used: 
```
# roll signer back to previous signing key
kubectl set env deploy/auth-signer SIGNING_KEY_KID=def456 -n auth
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-signer -n auth
kubectl rollout status deploy/auth-signer -n auth --watch
# verify
curl -s https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'
# monitor
kubectl logs -l app=auth-proxy -n ingress --since=10m | grep "JWT_VERIFY ERROR" | wc -l
```

Darren O'Neal: adding: create an alert for jwks-uploader error rate and add a sanity check in CI that ensures upload success before promoting signer changes.

incident-bot: Incident 1923509012 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Duration: ~44m.

Alex Chen: Handoff to Sam Patel for monitoring. Sam, I'm leaving detailed notes in the incident doc.

Sam Patel: Taking over monitoring. Will keep Slack channel open and will escalate if anything recurs.

Julie Park: I'll start drafting postmortem with impact numbers and customer communications.

security: please include verification of KMS audit logs for any access around the rotation time.

Alex Chen: Agree. We'll run KMS audit, jwks-uploader logs, and deployment pipeline logs for the postmortem. Thanks everyone and good catch. :thumbsup:
